study_material.title: Vocabulary - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Vocabulary questions test word meaning in context: fill in the blanks, one-word substitution, and commonly confused word pairs. Building vocabulary through roots and confusable pairs beats memorising isolated definitions.
learning_objectives: Choose words that fit both meaning and context
Use roots, prefixes and suffixes to infer unknown meanings

concepts.heading: 1. Commonly Confused Pairs
concepts.body: Accept (receive) / Except (excluding). Affect (verb: influence) / Effect (noun: result). Principal (head, main) / Principle (rule). Stationary (not moving) / Stationery (writing material). Complement (completes) / Compliment (praise). Eminent (famous) / Imminent (about to happen). Advice (noun) / Advise (verb). Lose (misplace) / Loose (not tight).

concepts.heading: 2. One-Word Substitution
concepts.body: A person who loves books = bibliophile. One who eats everything = omnivore. Study of birds = ornithology. A speech to oneself = soliloquy. Fear of water = hydrophobia. One who knows everything = omniscient. Government by the people = democracy. A cure for all diseases = panacea. One who is new to a field = novice. Words that read the same backwards = palindrome.

concepts.heading: 3. Suffixes Signal Part of Speech
concepts.body: -tion, -ment, -ness, -ity make nouns. -ous, -ful, -ive, -able make adjectives. -ly usually makes adverbs. -ise/-ize, -ify, -en make verbs. In fill-in-the-blank questions, the required part of speech eliminates half the options immediately.

concepts.heading: 4. Context Clues
concepts.body: Contrast clues follow 'but', 'however', 'although' - the blank opposes the earlier idea. Cause-effect clues follow 'because', 'therefore', 'so'. Example clues follow 'such as', 'for instance'. Read the FULL sentence before choosing; the clue often sits after the blank.

concepts.heading: 5. Collocations
concepts.body: Certain words habitually pair: 'heavy rain' (not strong rain), 'strong coffee' (not powerful coffee), 'make a decision', 'do homework', 'take a risk', 'pay attention', 'keen interest', 'bitter cold'. Placement papers often test these natural pairings.

formulas: Contrast words (but, however) signal an opposite in the blank
shortcut_methods: Identify the needed part of speech from the sentence frame first
Look for the signal word (but/because/therefore) to fix direction
Test each option by reading the complete sentence aloud mentally
common_mistakes: Ignoring the signal word and choosing a word of the wrong polarity
Picking a word with correct meaning but wrong collocation
study_material.summary: Fix the part of speech, read the signal word for direction, then choose the option with the right meaning AND the natural collocation.
quick_revision_notes: 'But/however' flips the direction of the blank
Heavy rain, strong coffee - collocations matter

solved_examples.question: Fill in the blank: 'The new policy will ___ all employees.'
solved_examples.step_by_step: A verb is needed after 'will'. 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is normally a noun.

solved_examples.question: One word for 'a person who loves books':
Fill in the blank: 'He is the ___ of the school and a man of high ___.'
solved_examples.step_by_step: The head of a school is the 'principal'; moral rules are 'principles'.
solved_examples.shortcut: The principAL is your PAL; a principLE is a ruLE.

solved_examples.question: Fill in the blank: 'Although the task seemed simple, it proved surprisingly ___.'
solved_examples.step_by_step: 'Although' signals contrast with 'simple', so the blank needs an opposite - complex.
solved_examples.shortcut: Contrast signal words demand opposite-direction answers.

solved_examples.question: One word for 'a remedy for all diseases':
solved_examples.step_by_step: PAN (all) + ACEA (cure) = a universal remedy. An antidote counters one poison; a placebo has no active effect.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Please ___ my apology.'
Fill in the blank: 'The car remained ___ at the signal.'
practice_questions.explanation: Stationary means not moving; stationery means writing materials.

practice_questions.question: One word for 'the study of birds':
Choose the natural collocation: '___ rain forced the match to be abandoned.'
practice_questions.explanation: 'Heavy rain' is the standard English collocation.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The medicine had no ___ on his fever.'
practice_questions.explanation: A noun is needed after 'no' - effect is the noun meaning result.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Because he had prepared thoroughly, he felt ___ before the interview.'
practice_questions.explanation: 'Because' signals a consistent cause-effect direction - preparation leads to confidence.

practice_questions.question: One word for 'a speech made to oneself':
practice_questions.explanation: SOLI (alone) + LOQU (speak). A monologue has an audience; a soliloquy does not.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'She gave me valuable ___ about my career.'
practice_questions.explanation: Advice is the noun; advise is the verb. Advice is uncountable.

practice_questions.question: One word for 'one who knows everything':
practice_questions.explanation: OMNI (all) + SCIENT (knowing). Omnipotent is all-powerful; omnipresent is everywhere.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The witness gave a ___ account, omitting no relevant detail.'
practice_questions.explanation: 'Omitting no relevant detail' defines the blank as complete and thorough.

topic_test.title: Vocabulary - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for correct, -0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
Identify the required part of speech and the signal word before choosing.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Everyone attended ___ Ramesh, who was ill.'
One word for 'a person who eats both plants and meat':
Fill in the blank: 'Don't ___ your keys again.'
questions.explanation: 'Lose' is the verb; 'loose' means not tight.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The scientist is an ___ authority in genetics, respected worldwide.'
questions.explanation: Eminent means distinguished; imminent means about to happen.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The two colours ___ each other beautifully in the design.'
questions.explanation: Complement means to complete or go well together; compliment is praise.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Despite his wealth, he lived a remarkably ___ life.'
questions.explanation: 'Despite his wealth' signals contrast, so the blank must mean simple or plain.

questions.question: One word for 'a word or phrase that reads the same backwards':
Fill in the blank: 'His argument was so ___ that even his critics were persuaded.'
questions.explanation: Cogent means clear, logical and convincing - matching the persuasive effect described.
